title: Hybrid Connectivity Decision Cheat Sheet — Request & Control Flow
purpose: Traces 99.99% High Availability Interconnect Topology Flow: 2 metropolitan colocation facilities, 4 physical cross-connects, dual Cloud Routers, and dynamic BGP route propagation.
routing_rationale: Achieving Google's 99.99% Interconnect SLA requires total physical diversity: two distinct colocation sites with redundant connections to two Cloud Routers.

nodes.label: On-Premises Edge Router 1
nodes.detail: Connects to Google Colocation Facility 1 (e.g. Equinix Ashburn).

nodes.label: On-Premises Edge Router 2
nodes.detail: Connects to Google Colocation Facility 2 (e.g. CoreSite Reston).

nodes.label: Google Metro Facility 1
nodes.detail: Carries Primary VLAN attachments to Cloud Router A.

nodes.label: Google Metro Facility 2
nodes.detail: Carries Secondary VLAN attachments to Cloud Router B.

nodes.label: Dual Regional Cloud Routers
nodes.detail: Propagates VPC subnets to on-premise network and dynamically fails over in < 3 seconds.

steps.title: Dual-Metro Physical Cross-Connects
steps.action: Provisions redundant physical circuits across two distinct metropolitan areas.
steps.why_traversal: Protects against localized fiber cuts or datacenter power outages.

steps.title: Dynamic BGP Route Exchange
steps.action: Cloud Routers exchange routes via eBGP; if Metro 1 fails, Metro 2 takes 100% traffic.

scenarios.label: Single Colocation Facility Violates 99.99% SLA
scenarios.root_cause: Customer deployed 4 cross-connects inside a single colocation facility to save cost.
scenarios.diverted_path: Google denies 99.99% SLA claim when facility power glitch caused outage.
scenarios.recovery: Mandate dual distinct metropolitan colocation facilities for all 99.99% SLA architectures.
